title: Project layers and finer kinds
summary: A project adds its own layers in cornfield.config.js as data (add, off, order; a match on type, kind, parent and field values), each node in exactly one layer, refused by name when wrong; a node's finer kind shows as letters in its core, in the legend, the badge and search, and a theme colours or gives an icon to a kind or a project layer. The persona node is an archetype for the scenarios, not something to build.

add.label: layers.js
add.desc: Pure: the layers config's checks and the matcher. The starting layers as entries of the same shape, and which one layer each node is in: the first project layer that takes it, else its starting layer.

set.desc: Reads and checks cornfield.config.js, now with layers: { add, off, order }, refused by name when wrong.

change.why: a project cannot add its own layers; the config refuses the key (#150)

set.desc: validate, now also warning about a project layer that matches no node or whose nodes an earlier layer took.

change.why: a layer that matches nothing would otherwise be silent

set.desc: The theme config, with icon keys by type, by type:kind and by layer:key, and the map contrast check over kind and project-layer tokens.

change.why: a theme can colour and give an icon to a finer kind or a project layer (#175)

set.desc: The Layers menu: project and starting layers in one order, counts that add up, All and None, overlays apart, the kinds of a type as key rows, the viewer's changes kept.

change.why: the rows are a hard-coded array and the chip counts an overlay as a layer (#150, #206)

set.desc: The scene: a node is drawn when its one layer is on, and always while a proposal it is in is open; a node's finer kind is drawn as letters in its core.

change.why: a timer, a webhook and a job look the same everywhere but one panel row (#175)

set.desc: The map's tokens, adding --corn-map-kind-<type>-<kind> and project --corn-map-group-<key>, most specific first.
The node panel, its badge naming the type and the finer kind: Service · timer.

change.why: the kind shows only in a row that wraps mid-word (#175, #207)

scenarios.title: The maintainer adds a layer for what runs on a clock

steps.text: The maintainer adds layers.add with key timers and match { type: service, kind: [timer, scheduler, job] }, off by default.
The checks pass; a typo such as type servce would be refused by name, with the node types listed.
validate reads the map: the layer takes 24 services, so it is not empty.
Layers shows Timers and schedules, 24, off; Services now counts 34; the chip counts layers, not overlays.
Turning it on draws the 24, each with its kind's letter in its core.

scenarios.title: The maintainer gives one finer kind its own colour in the theme

steps.text: The theme sets --corn-map-kind-service-timer; it wins over the layer's and the type's colour.
validate checks it at 3:1 on both grounds, and warns about a token for a kind that is not on the map.
Selecting one, the badge says Service · timer.
